session.title: Anchors Away (Permanently)
session.summary: The party murdered the rest of the crew, tried to cover it up, and then lost the ship anyway when a botched wake-up call sent Phineas, Alexander, and the anchor overboard.
recap: The session picked up mid-cover-up: with four stolen heart fruits needing replacements and a growing pile of corpses from last session's 'charitable' crew incident, the party decided the cleanest solution was to harvest hearts from the dead to disguise the theft, then dump the bodies overboard once the ship docked. Alexander loaded cannonballs into the hammocks of the deceased (Forehead, Butt Stuff, Fishfucker, and Skidmark) to weigh them down for a later burial at sea, while Phineas drew the short straw and was sent up top with Galen to deal with the ship's remaining problems: Hairbrush at the helm and an unmet, increasingly suspicious captain.

Before the heart-harvesting wrapped up, Gravestone - the blind gunner, already rattled by the chaos - woke up and nearly went for a weapon. Calazar tackled him silently, Alexander hit him with Command to freeze him in place, and the party tied and gagged him rather than add a fifth body to the pile. Meanwhile Alexander spent a very productive skill check scrubbing the poop-and-blood-covered stairs spotless (a recurring bit for the rest of the session), while Phineas skated gracefully through the muck on his way up to confront Hairbrush.

Topside, Phineas slapped a crayon-drawn map in Hairbrush's face trying to redirect the ship, only for the terrified helmsman to swat it away and abandon the wheel entirely, convinced the party was insane. Galen took over steering and Phineas took over navigation, with both of them rolling consistently excellent Survival checks to keep the ship on course toward port instead of the Rat Folk Kingdom. Calazar, meanwhile, had slipped into the captain's quarters and confirmed via stolen documents that the ship's true, secret destination really was the Rat Folk Kingdom.

Wanting a scouting edge, Phineas used an astral projection herb to send his soul up to the crow's nest - and his body immediately crumpled to the deck, unconscious for a full ten minutes. Galen, alarmed, tried slapping him awake, then force-fed him a goodberry (no effect on an unconscious target), then punched him once for good measure (it did not help). Growing desperate, Alexander carried Phineas to the railing to dunk him in seawater to wake him up, lost his grip, and watched his unconscious friend plunge into the ocean - so he dove in after him.

With the ship now sailing on without its paladin and cleric, Calazar tried to drop anchor to stop the ship and rescue them. The anchor rope snapped on a natural 1, violently jolting the entire ship, knocking Calazar prone, and dropping a stack of crates that crushed the tied-up, helpless Gravestone to death below deck. The noise also woke Captain Fishbone, who stormed out furious and immediately rolled initiative against Calazar and Galen.

The resulting firefight was brutal: Fishbone's gun shredded Calazar down to critical HP within a couple of rounds (he has an unfortunate glass-cannon 28 max HP), while Milo - arriving late to the chaos after hearing gunshots - got dropped to 1 HP via a devastating max-damage crit before being revived with the party's dwindling goodberries. Milo spent much of the fight magnificently rage-baiting Fishbone (literally punching him repeatedly in the groin with sneak-attack-boosted damage while Calazar peppered him with crossbow bolts), eventually grappling him, feeding him poisoned shark meat, and ultimately hurling him bodily off the side of the ship into the sea near the cliffs.

In the chaos, Fishbone managed one last petty act of revenge: his thrown sword missed Milo but struck a powder keg, which detonated and sent the unmanned, veering ship on a near-collision course with the rocky coastline. Only Milo noticed in time; a scramble of panicked dexterity saves kept everyone from being seriously hurt as the ship lurched hard to avoid the cliffs, finally settling into calmer, controllable sailing about 45 minutes into the 2-hour window before the point of no return.

Meanwhile, Alexander and Phineas were left floating in open water hundreds of feet behind the fleeing ship, with no way to catch up and no way to communicate with the others. With Phineas still unconscious and Alexander a famously bad swimmer, the two were effectively marooned and left to make their own way toward shore.

With the ship crew (and most of the original crew entirely) now reduced to Galen, Milo, and Calazar aboard and steering toward port, and Alexander and Phineas stranded separately in the water, the group decided to split the next two sessions: one following Galen and Milo (and presumably Calazar) continuing on the ship toward the previously-planned halfway-point town, and one following Alexander and Phineas making their way through the wilderness on foot - mirroring the overland route the party originally considered back in session 1.
highlights: Galen's natural 20 cooking roll charmed Captain Fishbone at the start of the session.
Phineas rolled an 18 Charisma save worth of pure aura, gliding completely untouched through a staircase coated in blood, poop, and piss.
Alexander scored a sparkling 19-22 on cleaning checks to scrub the crime-scene stairs spotless - twice.
Phineas smoking an astral herb immediately before danger and faceplanting his body for ten full minutes, directly kicking off the whole overboard disaster.
Milo's relentless rage-baiting of Captain Fishbone, including repeatedly punching him in the groin with sneak-attack-boosted damage.
The anchor's rope snapping on a natural 1, crushing the tied-up Gravestone under falling crates and waking the captain.
Milo heaving Fishbone bodily over the side of the ship near the cliffs to end the fight.
session.cliffhanger: The ship sails on toward port with only Galen, Milo, and Calazar aboard (plus a traumatized Hairbrush hiding in the kitchen), while Alexander and Phineas are stranded hundreds of feet behind in open water with no way to catch up - the party is splitting into two groups for the next sessions.
decisions: The party chose to harvest hearts from the four crew they'd killed to disguise the theft of the stolen heart fruits, rather than use rocks or other weight substitutes.
They decided to dump the hidden corpses overboard only once the ship docked, rather than risk it mid-voyage.
The group opted to spare Gravestone by tying and gagging him instead of killing him.
The party agreed to split into two parallel sessions next: one following Galen/Milo/Calazar on the ship, one following Alexander/Phineas overland.
table_talk: Long tangent about in-world curse words across different Brandon Sanderson Cosmere books (Mistborn, Warbreaker, Elantris, Tress).
Extended bit about AI-generated party portraits all accidentally sharing the same hairstyle.
Debate over realistic cannonball weights for the corpse-weighing plan, including looking up historical naval gun calibers.
Joke about an 'Office'-style cutaway interview with Alexander explaining his poop-cleaning backstory as a mercenary.
Comparing Phineas's astral projection ability to Brook from One Piece carrying his skeleton around separately from his ghost.
Riffing on movie anchor-drop tropes and whether you'd just cut the rope instead of lowering it.
Milo and the table joking about getting a boat 'fixed' for free since Fishbone 'owes him a debt' for being saved from drowning.
DM revealing he'd already built a town map for a 'halfway point' originally meant for the abandoned overland walking plan, and is repurposing it now.
Discussion of Kale possibly guest-starring as a temporary NPC (like playing Hairbrush) during the split sessions.
uncertain: Was Milo's bonus-action unarmed strike against Fishbone officially ruled as using 'Action Surge' or just a standard bonus action? The table seemed unsure of the ruling themselves.

party_updates.name: Alexander Warden
party_updates.note: Spent much of the session as unofficial janitor, repeatedly acing cleaning checks on the gore-covered stairs. Lost his grip on unconscious Phineas while trying to wake him with seawater and dove overboard after him, leaving him stranded in open water far behind the ship by session's end. Kept one of the four heart fruits in his bag.

party_updates.name: Ghalen Mordecai
party_updates.note: Impressed the captain with a natural-20 lunch, then took over steering the ship after Hairbrush fled the helm in terror. Fought Captain Fishbone with crossbow shots and Hunter's Mark, and panicked when Phineas's astral projection caused his body to collapse. Holding three of the four heart fruits.

party_updates.name: Phineas Fernspark
party_updates.note: Delivered a crayon map to Hairbrush with maximum confidence and zero success, then used an astral projection herb mid-crisis, knocking himself unconscious for ten minutes and indirectly causing himself and Alexander to be swept overboard and stranded.

party_updates.name: Milo Dozewell
party_updates.note: Overslept yet again and had to sneak aboard via firefly form last session; this session he arrived late to the fight against Fishbone, got dropped to 1 HP by a brutal critical hit, got revived with a goodberry, then turned the tide by relentlessly rage-baiting and eventually grappling and throwing Fishbone overboard.

party_updates.name: Calazar Dorento
party_updates.note: Snuck into the captain's quarters and confirmed the ship's secret course to the Rat Folk Kingdom. Botched an anchor drop that snapped the rope, crushed Gravestone, and woke the captain, then took heavy gunfire from Fishbone and was knocked to critical HP in the ensuing fight.

npcs.name: Captain Fishbone
npcs.description: The ship's cook/crew-facing captain figure, previously charmed by Galen's cooking.
npcs.location: In the water near coastal cliffs
npcs.note: Woke up furious after the anchor incident, fought Calazar, Galen, and Milo in a running gun-and-sword battle across the deck, and was ultimately thrown overboard by Milo near the rocky coastline after being poisoned with shark meat. Last seen treading water and glaring at the departing ship - his death or capture was not confirmed.

npcs.name: Hairbrush
npcs.description: Rookie deckhand searching for his long-lost fiance.
npcs.note: Was forced to take the helm, panicked the whole time, got a crayon map shoved in his face by Phineas, fled from the wheel convinced the party was insane, and spent the rest of the session cowering in the kitchen.

npcs.name: Gravestone
npcs.description: Elderly blind gunner, previously knocked out by Alexander.
npcs.note: Woke up and nearly reached for a weapon, was tackled and intimidated into submission by Calazar and frozen by Alexander's Command spell, tied up and gagged - then crushed to death by falling crates when the anchor snapped.

npcs.name: Court
npcs.note: Referenced as already dead from the prior session's events; his heart and body were part of the cover-up handled this session.

npcs.name: Forehead
npcs.description: Helmsman and Court's younger brother, briefly inherited the quartermaster role before dying.
npcs.note: His corpse's heart was harvested to replace one of the stolen heart fruits, and his body was weighted with a cannonball and dumped overboard.

npcs.name: Butt Stuff
npcs.description: Deckhand who previously flirted with Alexander.
npcs.note: Corpse harvested for a replacement heart and disposed of overboard with a cannonball weight.

npcs.name: Fishfucker
npcs.note: Corpse harvested for a replacement heart and disposed of overboard.

npcs.name: Skidmark
npcs.note: Corpse harvested for a replacement heart and disposed of overboard.

quests.title: Dispose of the Stolen Heart Fruits Discreetly
quests.note: The party harvested hearts from four dead crewmates to disguise the theft and weighted their bodies with cannonballs for a planned burial at sea.

quests.title: Clear the Party's Name in Tomoro
quests.note: No direct progress this session, but the body count keeps climbing, making this an increasingly tall order whenever they return.

quests.title: Reach the Uncharted Landmass
quests.note: The party's attempt to redirect the ship toward the correct port (instead of the Rat Folk Kingdom) led to chaos: the crew is dead, the captain overboard, and the group now split between the ship and open water.

mysteries.title: Why is the ship really sailing to the Rat Folk Kingdom?
mysteries.clue: Calazar found documents and maps in the captain's quarters confirming the ship and its cargo were specifically sought out, with a course deliberately set for the Rat Folk Kingdom instead of the party's intended destination.

mysteries.title: Who is the ship's captain?
mysteries.description: Captain Fishbone turned out to be a crew-facing figure who cooked and interacted with the party, but it remains unclear if he is the same shadow-faced captain from session 1 who stayed hidden in his quarters, or a different individual entirely.

loot.description: Stolen beating heart fruits from the cargo hold, now replaced in the crate with harvested human hearts to hide the theft; three held by Galen, one kept by Alexander in his bag.
Papers and ledgers taken from Captain Fishbone's quarters proving the ship's secret course to the Rat Folk Kingdom.
A hand-drawn map Phineas used (unsuccessfully) to try to redirect Hairbrush's steering; slightly crumpled and torn after Phineas's astral-projection collapse, but later smoothed out.

kills.creature: Gravestone (killed by falling crates after anchor snapped)

quotes.speaker: Alexander
quotes.text: When you're a mercenary, you know, there's always a guy at the bottom of the totem pole, always cleaning up poop. That was me for a bit. Everybody's got to start there at some point.

quotes.speaker: DM
quotes.text: He has a Zorro moment where he opens his eyes in the last quarter second and just catches himself.

quotes.speaker: Milo
quotes.text: I hope he can swim better than you can pilot a ship.

quotes.speaker: DM
quotes.text: This ship destroyers. I've got it.

quotes.speaker: Table
quotes.text: Don't do drugs. Somebody might throw you overboard.

quotes.speaker: DM
quotes.text: He keeps hitting me in the dick.
